clue.text: Bias shown by writer with song

parts.note: a pen is the thing you write with, a crossword stock for writer
a chant is a simple sung melody

explanation.surface: A slanted outlook revealed by a songwriter's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or leaning towards something, a kind of bias.

clue.text: Judge having crooked ties with friend

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of ties are rearranged

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A judge with bent neckties, or a crooked judge in league with a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity is to estimate it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: MPs' incomes to get reformed? That's sound

indicators.note: reforming something reshapes it, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call for MPs' pay to be overhauled, judged a sensible idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get reformed' rearranges all of MPS, INCOMES and TO; 'That's' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Compos mentis is Latin for being of sound mind, legally sane.

clue.text: Welsh politician facing test without scruples

parts.note: AM stood for Assembly Member, a member of the Welsh Assembly
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A Welsh legislator who faces an exam lacks moral standards.
explanation.walkthrough: AM was the title of a member of the Welsh Assembly (now the Senedd); an oral is a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral describes someone with no moral sense at all, who has no scruples.

clue.text: Uninspiring volunteers on edges of marquee

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so this comes first

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dull bunch of volunteers hanging round the sides of a big tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is the UK's part-time volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame, used of a performance or story, means flat and lacking excitement.

clue.text: Find entry form limits this writer

indicators.note: the form bounds the other piece on both sides, enclosing it

parts.note: a coupon is a form you fill in to enter a competition
the setter referring to themselves gives me

explanation.surface: Locate the boundaries of a competition entry form, says the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon something is to find it by chance, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Token panel announcing trade?

definitions.meaning: a token is an indication or mark of something
a board above a shop saying what business is done there

explanation.surface: A coin-like token or a shopfront board advertising a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a symbol standing for something and a shop's display board are called by the same word.

clue.text: Investigation — or probe by religious class?

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain
to search is to probe or look into

explanation.surface: An inquiry, perhaps carried out by a scripture lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is the British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic investigation to establish facts.

clue.text: Unsuccessful trio pulled apart by a book have to take a 50% cut

indicators.note: pulling something apart breaks it up, so the letters of trio are rearranged
losing half means only the latter half of the word have is kept

explanation.surface: A failed threesome splits up over a book and must accept halved earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled apart' turns TRIO into ORTI; 'take a 50% cut' leaves VE, the second half of HAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An abortive attempt is one that fails to achieve its aim.

clue.text: Check vertical part of glass

definitions.meaning: to check a flow is to halt or restrain it
the slender upright between the bowl and base of a wine glass

explanation.surface: Inspect the upright section of a wine glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to restrain a flow and the thin upright of a wine glass.

clue.text: Steadfastness needed for each retired priest entering spiritual meeting

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

indicators.note: the reversed priest goes inside the meeting

parts.note: a seance is a gathering to contact the spirits

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a priest

explanation.surface: Patience is required for every elderly cleric attending a session with the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reads the priest's title backwards, and 'entering' places that inside the seance; 'retired' looks like elderly, not a turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Perseverance is persistence in a task despite difficulty, steadfastness of purpose.

clue.text: Teach recruit changes in style of building

indicators.note: changes says these letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to train a new recruit, who alters a building's design.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture can mean the particular style in which buildings are designed, as in Gothic.

clue.text: Three notes about misbehaving class — it's seen by staff?

indicators.note: the notes are placed round the other piece

parts.note: B, E and F are three of the musical notes A to G

indicators.note: misbehaving suggests unruliness, so the letters of class are scrambled

explanation.surface: Some notes on an unruly class, noticed by the school staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' scrambles the class, and 'about' wraps the notes round it. The staff is the musical stave, not school employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass clef is the symbol written at the start of a musical stave, or staff, for low notes.

clue.text: German woman supported by daughter in crime

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes last

parts.note: Frau is German for a woman or wife

explanation.surface: A German woman helped by her daughter in a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is the crime of deception for financial gain.

clue.text: Purse is genuine, we're told

indicators.note: we are told it, so it is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: pukka, from Hindi, is British slang for genuine or proper

explanation.surface: A handbag that is the real thing, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purse' looks like a bag but is the verb, to purse one's lips. Pukka is British slang for genuine, and in non-rhotic British speech it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To purse the lips is to draw them together into wrinkles, the same as to pucker them.

clue.text: Body of water in summer enlarged

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A lake that swelled during the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake or pond, an old English term common in place names.

clue.text: Spot change required in clue for 'tiny amount'

parts.note: a mole is a small dark spot on the skin

indicators.note: change says the letters of clue are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor asking for a clue to be altered to define a small quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule is the smallest unit of a compound, hence loosely a very small quantity.

clue.text: Intellectual support following fashion

parts.note: a bra is a supportive undergarment
in means fashionable, in vogue

explanation.surface: A thinker backing whatever is trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain is informal for a very clever person, an intellectual.

clue.text: Place for drinking and music, with money turning over

parts.note: bars are the measures into which written music is divided

indicators.note: turning over flips it, so the word is read backwards, upwards in a down light

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: A pub with live music where the cash changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place for drinking' looks like the bar alone, but it defines the whole answer; BARS comes from 'music'. 'turning over' turns LOOT into TOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar stool is a tall seat at a bar counter, where one sits to drink.

clue.text: Painful sensation in field with pressure gone

indicators.note: gone signals that a letter has left the word

parts.note: a pitch is a playing field
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Discomfort on a sports field once the pressure eases off.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritating skin sensation, here loosely called painful.

clue.text: Guy beginning to bet in confined area in card game

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosed space
to guy is to mock, the same as to rib

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man starts gambling in a cramped room over a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored with pegs on a board.

clue.text: Brood — and refuse?

definitions.meaning: a family of young animals born together
the noun, rubbish or discarded waste

explanation.surface: Puppies or rubbish, as if asking whether a new-born lot might be declined.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a set of animals born at one time and scattered rubbish.

clue.text: Salesman in ground cited as feeble

indicators.note: the salesman goes inside the other piece
ground means crushed up, so the letters of cited are rearranged

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman on the sales ground is cited as weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' scrambles cited, and 'in' puts the salesman inside the result; 'ground' looks like a place, not a mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means weakened by age or ill use, worn out and feeble.

clue.text: Artist very enthralled by, say, Persian neckwear

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so these sit inside

parts.note: a Persian is an example of a cat breed, as say signals
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter utterly captivated by a Persian scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian' looks like a rug or a person; 'say' marks it as one example of a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a scarf-like band worn round the neck, tucked into a collar.

clue.text: A cost to a Scot moving throughout the country

indicators.note: moving means shifting things round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The price a Scotsman pays for relocating across the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Coast-to-coast describes something spanning a whole country from one shore to the other.

clue.text: Acknowledge a set of five letters (not half)

indicators.note: half the word is not used, so its last three letters go

parts.note: the vowels A, E, I, O, U are the set of five letters

explanation.surface: Admitting that a five-letter group lacks half its members.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare or admit something openly, to acknowledge it.

clue.text: Staff in Cheshire town reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is heard aloud

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: The workforce in a Cheshire town, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Crewe is a town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England, famous as a railway junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is the staff working a ship, aircraft or job.

clue.text: Russian river in country with source obscured

indicators.note: a source is a beginning, so the first letter is hidden away

parts.note: rural means in the countryside

explanation.surface: A Russian river in the countryside whose source cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source' sounds like the river's spring, but it is the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a river flowing from the Ural Mountains through Russia and Kazakhstan to the Caspian.

clue.text: Group of people put back golf feature — a legal omission?

indicators.note: put back means reversed, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pool is a group of people available for work, as in a typing pool
a hole is what golfers aim for on the course

explanation.surface: A team reinstating a green on the golf course, perhaps unlawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap in the wording of a law that lets people avoid it.

clue.text: Comedian present with degree showing age

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A comic on stage with a university degree, looking old.
explanation.definitionFit: Withered means shrivelled and wrinkled, as from age.
